Hong Kong Ani-Com & Games Expo 2026 kicks off today (24th). As a long-standing summer event for Hong Kong residents, citizens were already waiting outside the Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre as early as 9am this morning. Those who won the first-prize ballot were arranged to enter at 10am, continuing the traditional "Reverse Intelligence Spin" segment. Multiple exhibition zones were immediately swarmed with crowds upon opening.

Mr. Ip, who attends every year, registered for the ballot for the first time this year and struck it lucky on his first attempt, winning the "first prize". Upon entering, he took part in the "Reverse Intelligence Spin" first, saying he wanted to carry on the tradition of Ani-Com. He then headed to the Sanrio booth to purchase Hong Kong-exclusive Egypt-themed "Cinnamoroll" and "Pompompurin" plush toys, budgeting around HK$1,000 today to grab his favourite items.

Mr. Ip, who was at the head of the queue, made his way to the Sanrio booth immediately after entering to buy the Hong Kong-exclusive Egypt-themed "Cinnamoroll" and "Pompompurin" plush toys, with a long queue forming at the booth.

Mr. Hung, also part of the first-prize group, said he has been attending since the age of six, and it has become a habit for over a decade. He joked that this year he could witness the "Reverse Intelligence Spin" up close. He mentioned that he has witnessed the evolution of the anime exhibition over the past decade or so, one aspect being the changes in the doujin (indie creator) exhibition booths. He said that when he was young he might not have visited them, but as he was exposed to more games, he discovered that Hong Kong's doujin creations were also developing in tandem, and in recent years they have even formed their own dedicated zone, allowing different people to pursue their favourite works. He said he would first browse the main exhibition hall to buy models and figures, and then head to the doujin festival venue.

Although he won the first-prize ballot, Mr. Hung believes the ballot system has its pros and cons: "They might have arrived very early, maybe queuing since 6am, but they still have to queue behind the 300 (positions). They might not be able to buy what they want."

At 10am this morning, first-prize winners were able to shop at their favourite exhibition zones ahead of the crowd. The longest queues were at booths of Hong Kong brand Hot Toys, Bandai's model section, and Sanrio. According to records, Ani-Com officially introduced the real-name registration ballot system in 2018 to prevent problems such as overnight queuing and ticket scalping by touts. At the time, 500 slots were available, but this has been narrowed to 300 in recent years.
